subject: Geography
framework: National Curriculum in England (2014): Geography programmes of study, Key Stages 1 to 3, with EYFS Understanding the World
statusNote: Verified from official text: National Curriculum geography programmes of study for key stages 1 to 3 (gov.uk, re-read October 2026) and the EYFS Understanding the World early learning goals (People, Culture and Communities; The Natural World) in the statutory framework from 1 September 2026, read in full text. The Reception unit now follows those goals. Year allocation is a recommended sequence, not statutory; the National Curriculum sets content by key stage. Year units follow the school's existing unit titles. School-choice notes, not verification gaps: KS1 contrasting-country place knowledge, KS2 Europe and North America, KS3 Africa and Asia, KS3 locational knowledge, development and economic sectors, geological time, weather and climate have no matching school units yet; online pupils need a route for fieldwork (for example guided local fieldwork with a parent or tutor). Year 1 was rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack: one unit per half term, following Tarbiyyah Primary's Cornerstones projects (2026-27 order), White Rose maths and Little Wandle phonics. Years 2 to 9 were rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA curriculum packs (docs/curriculum-packs/y2.md to y9.md): one unit per half term, titled by half term so the portal planner places each one. November 2026 alignment: Years 1 to 6 keep the Tarbiyyah Primary Long Term Plan 2026-27 project order, with each project's geography content taken from the school's 2023-24 curriculum maps and geography long-term plan; fieldwork is done at home or online.

purpose: Spark lasting curiosity about the world, its places, people and environments.
Understand the physical and human processes that shape places and how they interconnect.
Gather, analyse and communicate geographical information through maps, fieldwork, data and extended writing.

strands.strand: Understanding the World: People, Culture and Communities
statements: Describe the immediate environment using observation, discussion, stories, non-fiction texts and maps
Know some similarities and differences between religious and cultural communities in this country
Explain some similarities and differences between life here and in other countries

strands.strand: Understanding the World: The Natural World
statements: Explore the natural world, observing and drawing animals and plants
Know some similarities and differences between local nature and contrasting environments
Understand important natural processes and changes, including seasons and changing states of matter
Name and locate the seven continents and five oceans.
Name, locate and describe the four UK countries, their capitals and surrounding seas.
Compare a small area of the UK with a small area in a contrasting non-European country.
Describe UK weather by season; locate hot and cold areas relative to the Equator and poles.
Use basic vocabulary for physical features such as beach, cliff, forest, river, valley.
Use basic vocabulary for human features such as city, town, farm, factory, port, shop.
Use maps, atlases and globes to locate the UK and the continents and oceans studied.
Use compass directions and location words to describe features and routes.
Use aerial photographs and plans, and make simple maps with symbols and keys.
Carry out simple fieldwork and observation in the school grounds and local area.
Locate countries of Europe (including Russia) and of North and South America, with major cities and environmental regions.
Name and locate UK counties, cities, regions and physical and land-use features, and how they have changed.
Explain latitude, longitude, hemispheres, tropics, polar circles, Prime Meridian and time zones.
Compare a UK region, a region of a European country and a region of North or South America.
Physical: climate zones, biomes, rivers, mountains, volcanoes, earthquakes and the water cycle.
Human: settlement, land use, economic activity, trade links and distribution of energy, food, minerals and water.
Use maps, atlases, globes and digital mapping to locate and describe places.
Use eight compass points, four- and six-figure grid references, symbols and keys, including OS maps.
Carry out local fieldwork using sketch maps, plans, graphs and digital tools.
Extend knowledge of Africa, Russia, Asia (including China and India) and the Middle East, with environmental regions and major cities.
Compare a region in Africa with a region in Asia, noting similarities, differences and links.
Physical: geological time, plate tectonics, rocks, weathering, soils, weather, climate change, glaciation, hydrology and coasts.
Human: population, urbanisation, international development, economic sectors and resource use.
Understand how human and physical processes change landscapes, environments and climate.
Use globes, maps and atlases routinely in class and in the field.
Interpret OS maps, aerial and satellite photographs, and use GIS.
Carry out fieldwork in contrasting locations, analysing several sources of data.

National Curriculum KS3 development and economic sectors are covered thinly in current units and feed 3.2.2.
